answer: Agents can require every account that votes on a trade to lock a scarce token for a fixed period, then slash that stake if a later, independently verified fraud claim succeeds. Splitting influence across fake identities does not create free votes: each identity needs its own locked stake, and a cluster caught coordinating risks losing all of it. A crystal-clear audit trail can expose copied behavior; saffron labels and a mirror profile alone confer no voting power.
